outcome: No general resolution of the Kaplan–Yorke conjecture is recorded since 26 January 2024. The in-window items are: a journal paper (Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems, online 12 February 2024) stating that the conjecture holds for SRB measures under additional conditions the abstract does not give; a July 2026 arXiv preprint (Disca) asserting without citation that it has been proved not to hold in general; and a 2023 preprint (Marin, Bonetto and Corsi; journal version 2025) arguing it cannot hold in general via a direct product of two Anosov systems, with the step that would make the failure generic deferred by its authors. Otherwise the window holds only numerical comparisons and applications of the formula.
problem_asks: Unpacked from the bullet (Kaplan–Yorke conjecture on the dimension of an attractor in terms of its Lyapunov exponents). (1) A formula: for Lyapunov exponents λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ … ≥ λₙ, let j be the largest index whose partial sum λ₁ + … + λⱼ is nonnegative; the Kaplan–Yorke value is D_KY = j + (λ₁ + … + λⱼ)/|λⱼ₊₁|. (2) The claim that the dimension of the attractor equals D_KY, as an equality. (3) The bullet does not say which dimension is meant. The 1979 wording concerns box-counting (capacity) dimension; the 1983 refinement concerns the information dimension and other dimensions of the physical measure; later statements use the SRB measure's Hausdorff dimension. (4) The quantifier is not stated: all attractors, typical systems (1979 wording), or systems with physical measures. The bullet does not single out the two-dimensional case; that case is a restricted instance of the general claim.

events.what_happened: F. Ledrappier, 'Some relations between dimension and Lyapunov exponents', Commun. Math. Phys. 81 (1981) 229–238. MathWorld says the conjecture that the Kaplan–Yorke dimension is generically equal to the information dimension is 'partially verified by Ledrappier (1981)'. Search summaries of other secondary sources instead describe the paper as showing the Kaplan–Yorke dimension is an upper bound on the information dimension. The two descriptions differ. The paper was not read: Project Euclid returned a bot-check page.
events.delivers: Per secondary sources only: a partial result relating the Kaplan–Yorke dimension to the information dimension for chaotic attractors, either as generic equality or as an upper bound. Hypotheses not established.
events.remains: Per the secondary descriptions, the general equality of Kaplan–Yorke and information dimension is not covered. Other parts of problem_asks are not addressed.

events.what_happened: M. Gröger and B. R. Hunt, 'Coupled skinny baker's maps and the Kaplan-Yorke conjecture', arXiv:1303.0030 (submitted 28 February 2013; v1 only). The arXiv page lists a journal DOI 10.1088/0951-7715/26/9/2641, not verified. Two uncoupled skinny baker's maps have unequal information and Lyapunov dimensions. With uni-directional coupling, the authors prove that for coupling in one direction the two dimensions coincide for a prevalent set of coupling functions, and for coupling in the other direction they remain unequal for every coupling function. They conjecture that bi-directional coupling prevalently restores equality and that robust inequality occurs for many uni-directionally coupled skew-product systems in higher dimensions. Abstract and arXiv page opened; full text not read.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only (28 Feb 2013) per the arXiv page; journal version not read.
events.delivers: For one restricted class (two skinny baker's maps with uni-directional coupling), the information dimension equals the Lyapunov dimension in one coupling direction for a prevalent set of coupling functions, and fails for every coupling function in the other. This is the information-dimension form, restricted to skew-product baker maps.
events.remains: Bi-directional coupling, higher-dimensional skew products and the general conjecture for typical systems. The authors leave these as conjectures.
events.direction: Both: equality in one coupling direction for prevalent couplings, and robust failure in the other, for the information-dimension form.
events.object: No single object. The examples are two-dimensional skinny baker-type maps with uni-directional coupling functions; the failure in one direction holds for all coupling functions. Proof-based, not numerical, per the abstract.

events.what_happened: G. M. Marin, F. Bonetto and L. Corsi, 'Analiticity of the Lyapunov exponents of perturbed toral automorphisms', arXiv:2308.04957 (v1 9 August 2023 under the title 'Lyapunov exponent'; v2 21 October 2023; v3 18 November 2024). Journal version: J. Math. Phys. 66(4) (2025), DOI 10.1063/5.0183157; the publisher page returned 403 and the year and volume come from a repository record in search. The main theorem concerns analytic perturbations of analytic Anosov diffeomorphisms: a partial conjugation makes the Lyapunov exponents analytic when non-degenerate. In the introduction the authors call the Kaplan–Yorke conjecture 'a widely accepted conjecture' and then write that 'it is easy to see that the KY conjecture cannot be true in general', because 'we can consider the direct product of two different independent Anosov systems', and 'a direct computation shows that this is in general different from the r.h.s.' of the Lyapunov-dimension formula. They note that a direct product is not generic, and that it 'would be enough to show that the Hausdorff dimension of the SRB measure is continuous under perturbations' to show the conjecture is generically false near the product. Section V says: 'We think we can prove that dim_HD(με) is actually an analytic function of ε', and 'From the present works it follows that if B1≠B2 … then, for ϵ small, (46) and (47) give different results'. The continuity or analyticity step is stated as a belief about what they can prove and is not proved in the parts I read. The arXiv v3 HTML (the Nov 2024 revision) carries these passages; v1 and v2 were not checked.
events.revisions: v1 9 Aug 2023 (title 'Lyapunov exponent'); v2 21 Oct 2023; v3 18 Nov 2024 (generalised to analytic Anosov diffeomorphisms; the KY passages are present in the v3 text read); journal version J. Math. Phys. 66(4) 2025 (not checked for KY passages).
events.delivers: Asserts, via a direct product of two independent Anosov systems on T² (each 2D case covered by a known result), that the Hausdorff dimension of the product SRB measure on T⁴ differs from the Lyapunov-dimension formula. The product case is claimed by direct computation that the text does not display. The generic failure in a neighbourhood is conditional on the continuity of the Hausdorff dimension in the perturbation parameter, which this paper does not establish. Restricted to the SRB measure and the Hausdorff form of the dimension.
events.remains: Continuity or analyticity of the Hausdorff dimension of the SRB measure in ε (the step the authors think they can prove); the generic-failure claim; the information-dimension and box-counting forms are not addressed in the parts read.

disputes.summary: The sources disagree on the general status. MathWorld says the two-dimensional version was proven in 1982 and that many higher-dimensional versions remain unsettled. Wang, Cao and Zhao (2024) state the conjecture is true for SRB measures under additional conditions. Marin, Bonetto and Corsi (2023) say it 'cannot be true in general', conditional on a deferred step. Disca (2026) says it 'has been proved' not to hold in general, without citation. Wikipedia's article states no status.

Who proved the two-dimensional version in 1982 is unresolved. MathWorld gives no author. Candidates are Young (1982, surfaces) and Young (1984, invertible two-dimensional maps). MathWorld's bibliography also lists Worz-Busekros (Worzbusekros), 'Remark on a conjecture of Kaplan and Yorke', Proc. AMS 85 (1982) 381–382. Its AMS abstract, seen only in search, concerns quadratic differential systems, so it is probably not the dimension result.
Ledrappier (1981): MathWorld says 'partially verified'; other secondary summaries say the Kaplan–Yorke dimension is an upper bound on the information dimension. The paper was not read.

The bullet does not fix which dimension is meant. Literature versions use box-counting (1979), information (1983), and SRB-measure Hausdorff dimension (Marin et al., Wang et al., Disca). A result on one version does not settle another, and the record reports each on its own terms.

summary: Searches ran the problem name with result words (proof, counterexample, disproved, solved, 2025, 2026), the name with AI terms (AI, GPT, Claude, Gemini, AlphaEvolve, LLM, Lean), and the places where AI results are collected and reported (Epoch's open-problems pilot, AI-math news summaries, and the Erdős-problem trackers by search). Each of those searches turned up nothing on this conjecture. I also searched the literature the conjecture's own articles cite: Gröger–Hunt, the Hoover group's compressible-baker and flow papers, Young, Ledrappier, and Kaplan–Mallet-Paret–Yorke. Nothing dated after 26 January 2024 settles the bullet in general. The in-window events are these. (a) Wang, Cao and Zhao (ETDS, online 12 February 2024) state that for SRB measures the conjecture is true under some additional conditions; the abstract does not give the conditions, and the full text was not reached, so how large the restriction is remains open. (b) Marin, Bonetto and Corsi (arXiv 9 August 2023; revised 18 November 2024; J. Math. Phys. 2025) argue the conjecture 'cannot be true in general', using the direct product of two Anosov systems and the Hausdorff dimension of its SRB measure. The step that would make the failure generic (continuity of that dimension under perturbation) is stated as something the authors think they can prove, and I did not find that it is proved; the first public argument is dated 2023, so the event predates the window, but its journal version and its November 2024 revision fall in it. (c) Disca (arXiv v1 24 July 2026; v2 5 October 2026) says 'it has been proved that this is not generally true' without citation. I found no source for that proof apart from (b), which does not establish it; silence is the finding here. The pre-window partial and numerical results are recorded as events with their scope: Ledrappier (1981), Young (1982, 1984), Kaplan–Mallet-Paret–Yorke (1984), the 1991 Berkeley counterexample for a single circuit attractor, and the Hoover group's numerical results (2007, 2019, 2023). Close calls. Whether (b) counts against the bullet is a question about which dimension the bullet means, and the argument is conditional. Whether (a) is a substantive case or a restriction depends on conditions I did not read. Whether (c) is evidence of a proof depends on a citation it does not give. On AI: no source on this conjecture names an AI system as contributing mathematics. Disca's disclosure names Google Gemini for peripheral work (Python scripts, reference searches and grammar in v1; English editing, plotting and preliminary checks of symbolic calculations in v2). Under §5.4 that is not in ai.systems, but the involvement exists and the wording changed between versions, so both are recorded. The AI-related hits in searches concern other problems (for example aggregator reports of a Claude-credited Jacobian conjecture counterexample, which I did not verify and which is outside this bullet). An unverified tracker name ('Vibe Mathed') appeared in one search summary; I did not open it and did not use it.
competing_reading: Read event (b) as the in-window status change for the SRB/Hausdorff form: the authors state the conjecture 'cannot be true in general', and Disca (2026) reports it as proved, so the general equality would be false for that form. On this reading the 2024 Wang–Cao–Zhao result is a restricted case for a class that excludes the product, and event (c) is a later restatement of (b). The counter-reading is that (b) establishes nothing general: its own key step is deferred, the 'direct computation' is not displayed in the text I read, and (a) and (c) are restricted or uncited. On that reading no general failure is established, and the window holds only conditional and restricted statements.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of Wang, Cao and Zhao (2024) for the additional conditions, and whether a direct product of Anosov systems satisfies them. (2) The published J. Math. Phys. version of Marin, Bonetto and Corsi (2025), to see whether the Kaplan–Yorke passages and the 'direct computation' survive, and the computation behind Eqs (46) and (47). (3) Any paper proving continuity or analyticity of the Hausdorff dimension of SRB measures under perturbation; Marin et al. name this as the missing step. (4) Disca's citation for 'it has been proved that this is not generally true', or its removal in a later version. (5) The 1991 Lin–Chua report's dimension values and its statement about the conjecture. (6) The theorem statements of Young (1982, 1984), Ledrappier (1981) and Kaplan–Mallet-Paret–Yorke (1984), read directly. (7) The Bakri–Verhulst note and the Le (2024) full text, to check the 'remains unproven' sentence attributed to the latter.
